messages.text: A and I both want the trailer in the next few weeks, and neither of us is backing down. B's pad is where it lives, so she is stuck in the middle. Can you help the three of us sort this out?

I need it to haul for my home project in the next few weeks. If I can’t use it then, my project gets held up. “I want to be able to use the trailer for my project without waiting for A to finish.” That fits.
I’d rather have the trailer out of my way, though I feel a bit bad asking since I agreed to keep it here. I also need to check with my landlord before changing what’s kept on the pad.
I can’t confirm either for B—she should say whether they fit. I don’t know what her landlord requires.
I want the freedom to take the trailer on weekend trips in the next few weeks; if it’s delayed, I may miss those trips. That’s accurate for me.
The first two fit. The third is close, but I’d put it as: “I feel torn about asking for the trailer to be moved, since I agreed to keep it here.”
No. I need it for hauling on my home project, not weekend trips: “I want to use the trailer for my project in the next few weeks without waiting for A to finish.”
Fine, but I need a concrete plan soon. I’m not waiting for A to finish before I use it.
Nothing beyond the trips. I’m not saying we need to fight over who goes first; we just need to work out a schedule soon.
(a) could work if I get the trailer for my project soon, without waiting for A to finish. Alternating weeks could hold me up. I can’t agree to a schedule until we pin down the handoff and dates.
Item 5 is accurate. No other concerns to add; I want us to settle a schedule soon so I can take weekend trips.
